display.title: Simcha and the Tzemach Tzedek
display.summary_short: The Tzemach Tzedek taught that acting happy brings real joy. A Chassid who forgot the richest poritz's seeds follows that advice, and a storm turns his trouble into blessing.
display.summary_long: The storyteller opens with a letter to the Tzemach Tzedek from someone who felt sad for no reason: think happy thoughts, speak happy words and act happy, and real joy will follow. He tells how the Baal Shem Tov found a man's lost oxen by looking in the Zohar, and teaches from the Zohar on Parshas Tetzaveh that Heaven looks at a person's face before giving blessing, which the Rebbe often quoted. Then the story: Rabbi Moshe, a wealthy Chassid who gives maaser where the Tzemach Tzedek advises, sells seed grain to the poritzim, who demand delivery on an exact day at a roadside inn. One year, halfway there, he realizes he forgot the chief poritz's special seeds and fears ruin. To his helper Shimshon's amazement, he begins to sing a happy niggun and clap. At the inn he buys strong drinks for all the poritzim, who drink until they fall asleep. A storm that night ruins every sack, yet the poritzim pay in full and order again. Rabbi Moshe explains the Tzemach Tzedek's parting words, 'Ki v'simcha seitzei'u': with joy you will go out of trouble.
display.lesson: Be b'simcha always, and even more when there is a problem; if you are not in the mood, act happy and the joy will come, bringing Hashem's blessings.

advisories.note: The hero buys strong drinks for the poritzim until they are drunk and fall asleep.

characters: Rabbi Moshe, a wealthy seed merchant
